content:
We're back with another round of picks from Apple official certified refurbished store. As a way to save money on iPhone, MacBook, Studio Display, and Apple TV becomes more and more popular, what we're talking about is definitely not the kind of iPhone that is "some guy's cousin's homemade and resold"—Apple's "strict refurbishment process" is fully present, and comes with a full one-year Apple warranty.

Click the link to see the selections we've already added to our shopping cart this week—iPhone, MacBook, Studio Display, etc.

Apple Refurbished Store—Weekly Picks

***Apple Certified Refurbished product inventory may be very limited

Justin—iPhone 16 Plus, Pro and Max

You can certainly find a cheaper iPhone 16 Pro on Amazon Renewed, but if I were buying a refurbished iPhone, I'd personally lean towards one with Apple official certification. Apart from AirPods, iPhone is arguably the most easily damaged among Apple's most commonly used products, so I'd go straight to the source and buy an unlocked refurbished iPhone with a full one-year Apple warranty.

Apple's refurbished store has quite a few 16 series models—if you ask me, this phone will remain competitive for years to come—from US$699, but what caught my eye is this 1TB 16 Pro Max going for US$1,269. That's US$330 cheaper than the equivalent 17 Pro Max, and US$130 less than the 512GB 17 Pro.

  • Refurbished iPhone 16 from US$699 (up to US$330 cheaper than the 17 series)

Chance—MacBook Air

MacBook Air is the model I always recommend to friends around me when they're buying a new Mac. It comes in 13-inch and 15-inch (my favourite) screen sizes, with plenty of RAM and storage configurations to suit different workflows. Right now, the best place to find MacBook Air deals is Apple's refurbished store:

  • 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 1TB storage and 16GB memory: US$1,359 (original price for new unit US$1,599)
  • 15-inch M5 MacBook Air with 1TB storage and 16GB memory: US$1,529 (original price for new unit US$1,799)
  • ……And more configurations to choose from……

Zac—48GB RAM MacBook Pro

Want the most memory for the least budget? Apple's refurbished MacBook Pro lineup has five versions with built-in 48GB RAM. The 16-inch M4 Pro MacBook Pro is hands-down the top choice for high-memory needs (such as running local AI models), and it's priced well under US$3,000.

Other 48GB RAM configurations include newer, more powerful Apple Silicon, nano-texture displays, and more CPU and GPU cores. At US$2,719 for a 16-inch M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 48GB RAM, it's a real bargain for those with high memory demands.

Marcus—Studio Display XDR

After a long wait, the Apple Studio Display XDR has finally gone on sale in the official certified refurbished store. Although this monitor dodged Apple's recent price hikes, it was never exactly cheap to begin with. So a roughly 15% refurbished discount really comes at the right time, especially for anyone looking to upgrade their desk setup with one of Apple's 27-inch 5K displays—it supports P3 and Adobe RGB colour gamuts, and has a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Refurbished Studio Display XDR—Standard Glass—VESA Mount Adapter: US$2,459 (original price US$2,899)
  • Refurbished Studio Display XDR—Standard Glass—Tilt and Height Adjustable Stand: US$2,799 (original price US$3,299)
  • Refurbished Studio Display XDR—Nano-texture Glass—Tilt and Height Adjustable Stand: US$3,059 (original price US$3,599)

Jeff—Apple Studio Display

The Studio Display XDR mentioned above is certainly the more attractive of the two monitors Apple currently sells, but the standard Studio Display can be picked up for US$1,100 cheaper at Apple's refurbished store, compared to the high-end version.

What's the main selling point of the standard Studio Display? It features a minimalist all-metal plus glass design. Although it lacks high refresh rate support, AdobeRGB and mini-LED backlighting, it has recently been upgraded to dual Thunderbolt 5, enabling daisy-chain setups. In terms of value for money, it's by no means the most affordable monitor, but in terms of design, it really stands in a class of its own.

  • Refurbished Studio Display—Standard Glass—Tilt Adjustable Stand: US$1,359 (original price US$1,599)

Ben—MacBook Neo

MacBook Neo is the newest addition, and for many people it's already sufficient for daily use. It got a US$100 price hike shortly after launch, but buying through Apple's refurbished store brings it back to the original price.

  • Base model (without Touch ID): US$599 (original price for new unit US$699)
  • Touch ID model: US$679 (original price for new unit US$799)
  • The links above are for the silver version, but you can find all colour options here
